label: Tech Startups (General)
description: Early-to-growth stage technology startups across non-SaaS verticals — marketplaces, fintech, healthtech, proptech, and other venture-backed tech companies. These properties are typically pre-content-maturity, built on modern frameworks, and navigating the zero-to-one SEO journey where foundational decisions have outsized long-term impact.

defining_seo_characteristics.primary_content_type: Landing pages, blog content, marketplace listings, product pages, industry thought leadership
defining_seo_characteristics.typical_conversion_path: Blog/thought leadership → product landing page → signup/waitlist → activation
key_seo_challenges: Category creation — targeting keywords for a product category that may not exist yet
Low domain authority competing against established incumbents for head terms
Resource constraints forcing brutal prioritization of content investment
Rapidly pivoting product direction invalidating existing content strategy
Marketplace cold-start problem — no listings means no organic content means no traffic means no listings
key_seo_opportunities: First-mover advantage on emerging category keywords before competition saturates
Thought leadership content establishing the founder/team as category authorities
Programmatic content from marketplace or platform data (if available)
PR and launch content generating high-authority backlinks early
Community-driven content seeding organic growth before paid channels scale

fleet_intelligence_notes.cross_industry_transfer: Moderate. The zero-to-one SEO trajectory shares common patterns across all startup verticals — foundation building, initial authority acquisition, first content clusters. Industry-specific patterns diverge as startups mature into their vertical.
fleet_intelligence_notes.protocol_sequencing_pattern: Typically: Index Diagnostic → Content Opportunity → Meta Surgeon → Link Architecture. Startups often have technical foundations in place (modern frameworks with good defaults) but minimal content and authority. Content strategy comes before link architecture because there must be something worth linking to.

industries.label: Marketplace Startups
industries.description: Two-sided or multi-sided marketplace platforms. The defining SEO challenge is the chicken-and-egg problem — listings create organic content, but organic traffic is needed to attract listings.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and local — users searching for specific services, products, or providers in a location
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Varies by vertical — established marketplaces (Airbnb, Upwork) have massive moats, but niche verticals are accessible

industries.label: Fintech (Non-SaaS)
industries.description: Consumer and business financial technology — neobanks, payment apps, lending platforms, and wealth management. YMYL territory requiring heightened E-E-A-T signals.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and commercial — consumers researching financial products and comparing rates
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High — NerdWallet, Bankrate, and traditional banks dominate broad terms. Niche fintech categories offer opportunity

industries.label: Healthtech (Non-SaaS)
industries.description: Consumer and provider-facing health technology — telehealth platforms, health apps, wellness tech. YMYL with strict quality requirements for health-related content.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and transactional — patients seeking health information and booking care
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High for broad health terms (WebMD, Healthline), moderate for specific healthtech services

industries.label: Proptech
industries.description: Property technology startups — tenant platforms, property management, real estate analytics, and construction tech. Geo-heavy SEO with strong programmatic content opportunities.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and informational — property searches combined with market research
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High for consumer real estate (Zillow, Redfin), lower for B2B proptech and construction tech niches

industries.label: Climate / Cleantech
industries.description: Climate technology, renewable energy, carbon accounting, and sustainability startups. Emerging category where content authority is being established in real-time.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — businesses and consumers researching climate solutions and regulations
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — category is nascent. Early content investment creates outsized long-term positions

industries.label: Mobility / Transportation
industries.description: Transportation technology — EV charging, fleet management, micro-mobility, and logistics platforms. Geo-specific content patterns combined with technology education.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and local — location-specific service discovery
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — fragmented across many sub-verticals with few dominant organic players per niche

industries.label: Media / Content Startups
industries.description: Digital media platforms, creator tools, and content distribution startups. SEO is existential — organic traffic is often the primary business model driver, not a support channel.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — readers seeking content on specific topics
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very high — media is the most content-competitive vertical. Differentiation requires either niche focus or original data

industries.label: Social / Community Platforms
industries.description: Community platforms, social networks, and forum-based products. SEO driven by user-generated content (UGC) indexation — the community IS the content.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational and navigational — users searching for specific discussions, communities, or topics
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — Reddit dominates broad community queries but niche communities compete effectively on specialized topics

industries.label: Insurance Tech
industries.description: Digital insurance platforms, comparison engines, and insurtech startups. YMYL territory with strong programmatic content opportunities around coverage types and geography.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Commercial investigation — consumers comparing insurance options and seeking coverage information
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High — Policygenius, The Zebra, and traditional carriers invest heavily in organic content

industries.label: Travel / Hospitality Tech
industries.description: Travel booking platforms, hospitality management, and travel experience startups. Intensely geo-specific with massive programmatic content potential around destinations and properties.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and informational — travelers researching destinations and booking accommodations
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very high — Booking.com, TripAdvisor, Airbnb have enormous organic moats. Niche travel verticals offer opportunity

industries.label: Recruiting / Talent
industries.description: Recruiting platforms, talent marketplaces, and HR tech startups. Two-sided marketplace dynamics with job listing pages as the primary organic content layer.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Transactional and informational — job seekers searching for roles and researching companies
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Very high — Indeed, LinkedIn, Glassdoor dominate. Vertical-specific recruiting niches offer opportunity

industries.label: Govtech / Civic Tech
industries.description: Government technology, civic engagement platforms, and public sector tech startups. Unique SEO landscape — low commercial competition but complex stakeholder content needs.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — citizens seeking government services and policy information
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Low — government .gov sites rank well by default but rarely optimize, creating opportunity for well-optimized civic tech content

industries.label: Web3 / Blockchain
industries.description: Blockchain infrastructure, DeFi, NFT platforms, and Web3 startups. Rapidly evolving terminology creates constant keyword opportunity as new concepts enter public awareness.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — users seeking to understand emerging Web3 concepts and evaluate platforms
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — CoinDesk, CoinGecko dominate informational queries but platform-specific and emerging concept queries are accessible

industries.label: Personal Finance / Consumer Fintech
industries.description: Consumer financial apps — budgeting, investing, saving, and financial wellness tools. YMYL territory with massive informational content demand around financial literacy.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — consumers seeking financial education and tool comparisons
seo_patterns.competitive_density: High — NerdWallet, Investopedia have massive authority. Niche personal finance topics (FIRE, student debt, freelancer taxes) offer opportunity

industries.label: Legaltech Startups
industries.description: Legal technology startups disrupting traditional legal services — contract automation, legal marketplaces, compliance platforms. YMYL with opportunity in demystifying legal processes.

seo_patterns.dominant_intent: Informational — individuals and businesses seeking legal guidance and comparing services
seo_patterns.competitive_density: Moderate — LegalZoom and Rocket Lawyer dominate broad terms but specific legal domains have accessible long-tail
